text:
elena_marketing: Hey team :wave: — prepping slides and a short webinar demo for next week. Need the runtime team to produce a canonical set of inference outputs + methodology notes we can cite. Specifically: can eng/runtime run a small matrix of sample payloads and share sanitized raw logs, per-request latencies (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, and the exact config used (batch size, seq len, quant flags)? We want publishable numbers by EOW and a short README describing the methodology and any caveats.

kevin_runtime: Thanks — we can do that. Quick clarifying Qs: which model variants do you want in the matrix? Also which sequence lengths and batch sizes to prioritize? Are you after mean/p95/p99, or also per-token distributions? And do you need cost estimates mapped to our pricing?

elena_marketing: Good Qs. Start with two variants: redwood/13b-v2 (float) and redwood/13b-q4 (quant). Sequence lengths: 32, 128, 512. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8. Metrics: p50, p95, p99, tokens/sec, and an expected cost-per-1k-tokens estimate (use current hosted rates). Per-token distribution would be great if not too noisy. Please sanitize any request text (no customer data). Also include the prompt set (we'll attach it in this thread).

kevin_runtime: Got it. We'll run a smoke matrix with those combinations and return both CSV (summary rows) and a gzipped JSONL of raw runs. We'll include a README with: exact command line, kernels used, hardware (GPU model), docker image + runtime git commit, and the seed for determinism. Expect some variance across runs; we'll report run-to-run stdev. If load spikes, we can pin to a dedicated dev node for the run. Example run command we'll use:

```
# smoke run example
python infra/tools/run_inference_bench.py \
  --model redwood/13b-v2 \
  --seq-lens 32,128,512 \
  --batches 1,4,8 \
  --samples 50 \
  --out /tmp/marketing_matrix_v2.jsonl
```

aj_sre: Heads up — Dedicated dev clusters are booked for the next 48h for a deploy window. If you need guaranteed isolation, we should schedule for Friday lunchtime PST or use a preemptible staging node tonight. Also watch GPU quotas (NVIDIA A100 pool).

kevin_runtime: Thanks @aj_sre — we'll try staging first. If variance is too high we'll ask ops to spin a pinned node. For outputs we'll produce: CSV summary with columns: model, quant, seq_len, batch, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, samples_run, cost_per_1k_estimate. Raw JSONL will include per-request: {request_id, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, node_id, gpu_util_pct, kernel_name} — sanitized.

sam_analytics: For analytics ingestion please include these fields exactly so I can plug into the dashboard: request_id, timestamp, model, quant_flag, seq_len, batch_size, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, gpu_util_pct, mem_used_mb. CSV header matching is appreciated. We also need a short note on how you compute cost_per_1k_estimate (which price, which token counting method).

kevin_runtime: Will do. We'll attach both the sample prompts file and the run artifacts in this thread when done. Expect first smoke artifacts within ~6-8 hours, final polished README and CSV by EOW. Note: if we run on shared staging expect ~10-15% higher p95 vs dedicated.

deploy-bot: Scheduled bench job 1752468180 on cluster staging-bake-03 (ETA 10m).

elena_marketing: Amazing, thanks everyone — that timeline works. When you attach artifacts please also include a short one-paragraph recommended copy for the slide (one-sentence claim + caveat). That helps legal/comm sign-off. :thumbsup:

kevin_runtime: Will include the suggested slide copy and a short list of known caveats. Closing loop here — I'll post artifacts and a short changelog once runs finish.
